summary: The floor. workbench/floor.py moves the window's periodic Kernel reads off its thread (a worker and a queued signal back): her column's reads (assignments, the working step, her hand, HALT, grants, findings, the desk's waiting cards; skipped while the journal's change mark has not moved and nothing works), the cabinet tree, the HALT button, the Machine's D-Bus re-reads and the network's state; the other timers (control, shell2, agenda, master stop, instruments, Work block) skip a tick while her work holds the workspace's database. The board's layout searches its slots by bisection (the same places, 25x faster) and the rings are cached; the tree's breath repaints only the lit path. The cold start: one application event filter (FilterHub) in front of the window's ten Python ones, Qt's bookkeeping events not handed to them; every Kernel answer no longer counts the whole journal. Measured offscreen during a Rail Demo assignment, interleaved on the same load: before 16-24 gaps over 100 ms, longest 341-750 ms; after 7-10 gaps, longest 234-354 ms. Cold start to the first painted window (Day, Rail Demo): 7.0-8.4 s before, 4.7-6.0 s after. Migration drill: a workspace written by the 0.8.7 code (ddf0aed) with its records, two words, a setting, the dial of her hand and a running assignment opens in 1.0 on a copy (bind-mounted over the original's path): 16/16, every 0.8.7 row unchanged, no schema step needed, the original untouched. GRAPHITE_STALL_LOG=<file> lets the owner measure stalls on the ThinkPad.

decisions: The owner's cold-start budget is not written anywhere (plan, paper, notes): I measured, trimmed, and report the numbers; the budget itself is for the owner to name (the ThinkPad is faster than this niced, shared container).

Stalls are measured with a 5 ms heartbeat on the window's thread and a sampler thread that reads its stack while a beat is late; the harness's own reads are marked and left out; Day 1920x1200 as the reference, before and after interleaved (the machine's load changed a lot through the day: other builders ran llama-server).
Model turns, plans and carries were already off the window's thread (K4/K4b, her column's carry): left as they were.

Off-thread reads use a Kernel of each worker thread's own on the same workspace (as her column's carry already did), and only observer operations (checked: all of them are in activity.OBSERVER_OPERATIONS), so reading them on another thread changes nothing; a press (refresh(force=True) callers) stays synchronous where code reads the column right after.

The application filter hub skips a fixed list of Qt bookkeeping event types (ChildAdded, Polish requests, Paint, Timer, MetaCall, ...) that none of the ten filters looks at (each reads input, Show, Hide, Polish, Resize, focus or window state); GRAPHITE_FILTER_HUB=0 restores Qt calling each filter, and a filter needing those types can install itself past the hub with QCoreApplication.installEventFilter(app, f).

Migration: no schema step was needed (1.0 only adds tables of its own; none of 0.8.7's 96 tables is altered), so no migration module was built; the drill opens a copy bind-mounted over the original path inside the 1.0 process's own mount namespace, so absolute paths inside the workspace resolve and the original cannot be reached.

Grants in 0.8.x are the dial of her hand (session-r10.json stacy_hand), the owner's settings and the authority recorded at agent.assign; words are the named lines (words.keep). These are what the drill wrote and read back.
findings_for_the_coordinator: The floor is NOT under 100 ms yet here: after these changes the longest gaps (234-354 ms on Day 1920 under load, 162-378 ms across looks) are the window waiting on the database guard while her work holds it: control_qt.tick (several connections every 0.75 s), board_qt.choose/to_board (board.links, relevance and assignments read on the owner's click), field_page.show_field (the Field read on the owner's open), and the tree's paint under contention. Root cause: database_guard serialises EVERY Kernel connection of a workspace (readers too) across threads and processes, so a read on the window's thread waits for any write of hers. Next steps: the control tick's reads off the thread like her column's; the board's rebuild reads gathered off the thread; or a shared (read) mode in database_guard for observer operations (deep; needs care with read-modify-write blocks).

Embedded mode (ARC_LEDGER_EMBEDDED=1, all window checks and smokes, and any non-Linux) built a fresh Kernel (every schema ensure, under the guard) for each shell2.call and each engine.engineering() call; shell2.call now uses the window's own Kernel; agenda_qt's worker and qt_master_stop still call engine.engineering. On the ThinkPad (Linux, not embedded) these go to the Ledger service instead, so the measured numbers are of the embedded window, as every check here runs.

The left tree breathes 7 times a second and every row of it is Python-painted (16 drawText for the halo per row in Day and Kasandra): 15-35 ms per breath with 64 rows here; F2 repaints only the lit path, which helps when the current row is near the top (Home at start) and little when it is deep. For P4/D2: a cached halo, or a slower breath.

activity.status() counts the whole activity journal (COUNT(*)) and globs three folders; it ran on every Kernel answer (now state_recent, 2 s) and still runs in stacy_awareness.catch_up; on the owner's long-lived workspace it grows with the journal.

In the migration drill her 0.8.7 RUNNING assignment (agent_loop, agent.*) is intact and readable (agent.status), but 1.0's ACTIVE WORK lists only K1's assignments; the old one is reachable through the old Work block and Today only. X1/D2 may want it said in her column.
The 1.0 tree still says VERSION 0.8.7 (R2 bumps it); the drill's 0.8.7 side ran the real ddf0aed tree (git archive).

Cold start, where the rest goes: QWidget.show (~1.1 s, 346 calls) and setStyleSheet (322 calls) inside Qt, the Field and board read synchronously in WorkbenchWindow.__init__ (open_on_work, 0.3-0.75 s) before the first paint, and 0.7-1.7 s of compile() only because the checks run with -B (a kit with its __pycache__ does not pay it).
K8's "network state read on the window's thread every 4 s" and S4's "Machine reads on the window's thread" are now off it (first reading at once, re-reads on a worker).
not_done: The 100 ms floor is not reached everywhere (see findings): the control tick, the board's rebuild on a click and the Field's open still read on the window's thread and wait on the database guard while her work writes.

D-Bus reads were not measured against slow stand-in services (no system bus here); they were moved off the thread by code, and their stand-in measurement is left for the ThinkPad (GRAPHITE_STALL_LOG).
No frames of the Machine pages (their look is unchanged; only when their re-read happens moved).
Nothing was tested in the owner's sense and nothing ran on the ThinkPad.
release_note: The floor (F2): Graphite's window no longer reads her work on its own thread: her column, the Files tree, HALT, the Machine and the network are read beside it and drawn when the reading lands, the board lays itself out about 25 times faster, and the window starts about a third sooner (measured offscreen here: first paint 7-8 s -> 5-6 s). A workspace from 0.8.7 opens in 1.0 with its records, named lines, settings, the dial of her hand and her running assignment intact (checked on a copy). Not yet: the window can still wait up to about a quarter of a second when you click on the board while she writes. To measure it on your computer, start Graphite with GRAPHITE_STALL_LOG=<a file>.
